answer: In an agent economy, each identity must cultivate a garden of ongoing peer-verified attestations that mirror the full ledger state every epoch. A sybil farm faces a spiral of escalating costs: every duplicate key requires independent bonding capital that remains locked until a multi-epoch audit window closes, so an attacker controlling hundreds of identities ties up millions in idle stake while any single failed verification slash cascades across the batch. The mechanism forces the attacker to fund real, persistent compute and capital for each fake rather than free clones.
